newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power eases with mild temps, restarts.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power eases with mild temps, restarts.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were mostly softer Monday as warmer temperatures moved toward the region and a couple of nuclear plants returned to service, sources said.

Firm, peak power in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday delivery traded in the $22.00-23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Friday's $25.00 trading range.
TVA's 1,148 megawatt (MW) Sequoyah 2 nuclear unit in Soddy-Daisy, Tenn., is boosting power, and as of early Monday morning the unit was operating at 50 percent power.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission said an electrical problem resulted in the loss of two reactor coolant pumps, causing last week's shutdown.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was assessed in the $13.50-15.00 range, mostly unchanged from Friday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday delivery were quoted at $22.00-23.00 per MWh, down from the $25.00 trades seen on Friday.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed at $16.00-16.50.
Despite well-below normal temperatures today in the Southeast, temperatures are expected to rise to above-normal levels by Wednesday, with the warm trend continuing into the early part of next week.

Separately, Duke Power said the 1,129 MW Catawba nuclear power unit in Clover, S.C., returned to the electricity grid early Monday after the unit was shut last week due to a small leak in a reactor coolant pump.
